title: Interpreting Prophetic Writings
intro: November 14–20, 2026. In the great controversy, the conflict is not merely over whether we accept God's Word, but whether we understand it correctly, trust what it reveals about His character, and allow it to transform our lives.
heroQuote: Revelation must be correctly understood before it can produce the transformation God intends.

footer.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

themes.title: Revelation, Demonstration, and Understanding
themes.summary: God answers the great controversy's questions about His trustworthiness and character through revelation and demonstration. Correctly understanding His Word enables the transformation that makes His character visible in our lives.

themes.title: Jesus Grew in Wisdom Through Scripture
themes.summary: In His humanity, Jesus studied and lived by the Scriptures He had inspired. Taught by His mother and guided by God's Word, He grew in wisdom and prepared for His mission, temptations, and suffering.

quotes.quote: His mother was His first human teacher. From her lips and from the scrolls of the prophets, He learned of heavenly things. The very words which He Himself had spoken to Moses for Israel He was now taught at His mother’s knee.
quotes.author: Ellen G. White
quotes.source: The Desire of Ages, p. 70, paragraph 1 (DA 70.1)

themes.title: Jesus Discovered His Messianic Mission Through Scripture
themes.summary: The sacrifices, temple services, prophecies, and stories of Scripture illuminated Christ's mission. Their pictures of mediation, sacrifice, suffering, and redemption helped Him understand the work He came to fulfill.

themes.title: Jesus Recognized When the Time Was Fulfilled
themes.summary: The lesson connects Daniel's prophecy with the Messiah's appearance and anointing in AD 27. Jesus understood the appointed time for His ministry through the prophetic Scriptures.

themes.title: Jesus Learned From the Faith and Failures of Others
themes.summary: The lives of earlier believers supplied examples of faithfulness under trial and lessons from human failure. Their experiences anticipated and illuminated the challenges of Christ's own mission.

themes.title: Jesus Found the Great Controversy in Scripture
themes.summary: Biblical accounts of rebellion, suffering, deliverance, and judgment revealed the conflict between God and Satan. In His humanity, Christ became a student of the very stories and prophecies He had inspired.

themes.title: I. Interpret Scripture as a Unified Revelation
themes.summary: Jesus read Scripture as a coherent revelation of God's redemptive purposes and called His disciples to believe all the prophets. The lesson applies this principle to death and resurrection, interpreting Paul's desire to be with Christ alongside clearer passages about Christ's return.

themes.title: II. Recognize Historical Context and Stages of Fulfillment
themes.summary: Jesus distinguished the prophecy fulfilled in His present ministry from judgment still to come. Likewise, the lesson reads His warning about Jerusalem in its first-century setting while recognizing its broader significance for the end of the age.

themes.title: III. Let the Full Biblical Testimony Govern Interpretation
themes.summary: Satan used a promise of protection to tempt Jesus into presumption, but Christ answered with Scripture's prohibition against testing God. A faithful interpretation considers the whole biblical witness and never turns a promise into permission for recklessness.

themes.title: IV. Place Scripture Above Human Tradition
themes.summary: Jesus challenged traditions that displaced God's commandments and obscured His identity. Applying that principle to the Lord's day, the lesson identifies the seventh-day Sabbath as God's holy day through explicit biblical statements rather than inherited tradition.

themes.title: V. Recognize God's Character in His Law
themes.summary: Jesus showed that God's commandments address thoughts, motives, and love for others, including enemies. An interpretation that produces outward doctrinal conformity without Christlike love misses the law's purpose of reflecting God's character.

themes.title: VI. Be Willing to Obey the Truth
themes.summary: Jesus submitted to Scripture and the Father's revealed purpose even when obedience led to suffering and death. Faithful interpretation requires a willingness to obey God's truth rather than reshape it around personal preferences.

themes.title: Applying Christ's Principles to Ellen White's Writings
themes.summary: Read Ellen White's counsel in its historical and literary context and alongside her broader writings. Distinguish enduring principles from period practices, keep Scripture as the final doctrinal standard, and seek the restored relationship with God that prophetic counsel intends.

themes.title: Faithfulness in the Final Crisis
themes.summary: From Eden to the final crisis, Satan distorts God's Word to undermine trust and redirect worship. Following Christ's interpretive principles prepares believers to resist deception and reflect God's character, demonstrating the transforming power of His grace.
